question: In which of the following years was Subash Chandra Bose appointed as the President of the Indian Independence League?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1943**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Subhas Chandra Bose, a prominent leader in the Indian independence movement, was appointed as the President of the Indian Independence League in 1943.

• The Indian Independence League was a political organization that was formed to organize the Indian independence movement outside India.

• Bose's leadership of the Indian Independence League was instrumental in the establishment of the Indian National Army (INA), which aimed to secure India's independence from British rule.

• Under Bose's leadership, the Indian National Army fought alongside the Axis powers during World War II to liberate India from British colonial rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Subhas Chandra Bose:**

• Subhas Chandra Bose was a prominent Indian nationalist leader who actively fought for India's independence from British rule.

• Bose's approach to achieving independence was more radical and militant compared to Mahatma Gandhi's non-violent civil disobedience movement.

• He is known for his famous slogan "Give me blood, and I will give you freedom!"

• Bose's efforts and his leadership of the Indian National Army played a significant role in India's struggle for independence.

• **Indian National Army (INA):**

• The Indian National Army was formed by Indian nationalists in 1942 in Southeast Asia during World War II.

• It was initially founded by Captain Mohan Singh, but later re-organized and led by Subhas Chandra Bose.

• The INA sought to overthrow British rule in India with the help of Japan and other Axis powers.

• The INA's campaigns in Burma and India, although ultimately unsuccessful, inspired many Indians and contributed to the growing demand for independence.

• **Indian Independence Movement:**

• The Indian independence movement was a series of activities and efforts aimed at ending British colonial rule in India.

• It involved various strategies, including non-violent protests, civil disobedience, and militant campaigns.

• The movement saw the participation of numerous leaders, including Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, Subhas Chandra Bose, and many others.

• The movement eventually led to India gaining independence on August 15, 1947.
